kurzbeschreibung: East Tyrol is a sun-drenched alpine paradise between the majestic Hohe Tauern range with Mount Grossglockner and the rugged Lienz Dolomites.
beschreibung: East Tyrol (Osttirol, district of Lienz) is Tyrol's sunniest region and a haven for alpine enthusiasts. Surrounded by 266 three-thousand-meter peaks, the territory stretches from the vast Hohe Tauern National Park—crowned by Austria's highest summit, Grossglockner (3,798 m), and the Grossvenediger in the north—down to the limestone spires of the Lienz Dolomites and Carnic Alps in the south. The charming district capital of Lienz delights visitors with its Mediterranean flair, palm trees on the main square, and medieval Bruck Castle featuring artwork by Albin Egger-Lienz. Pristine valleys like Defereggental, Virgental, Kalsertal, and Villgratental preserve authentic mountain farming traditions away from mass tourism.
tipps: Visit the Umbal Falls in Virgental – Europe's first water-themed nature trail along the cascading Isel glacial river.
Taste authentic East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen and protected regional Pregler schnapps at local inns.
Hike the Kalser Höhenweg trail offering breathtaking vistas of the imposing Grossglockner south face.
empfehlungen: Explore the Hohe Tauern National Park on ranger-guided wildlife safaris in search of golden eagles and ibex. Afterwards, treat yourself to hearty regional cuisine at the spectacular Dolomitenhütte perched on a rocky cliff or at Lucknerhaus in Kals.
umgebung: East Tyrol is linked to North Tyrol via the Felbertauern Tunnel road. It borders Salzburg to the north, Carinthia to the east and south-east, and Italy (South Tyrol and Veneto) to the south and west. Key valleys include the Isel Valley, Drau Valley, Virgental, Defereggen Valley, and Villgraten Valley.
